**Confidentiality Schedule – Pilot for Unpublished Donor Letters**

**1. Subcontractor Processing**  
- External color specialist may receive master images for the first batch only.  
- Scope limited to color calibration; no donor text or metadata may be extracted or retained.  
- Specialist must sign a non‑disclosure agreement and return or delete all materials within 20 days of delivery.  
- Files retained for internal quality‑control review for up to 10 days after delivery; thereafter all copies must be destroyed unless otherwise approved.

**2. Master Images vs. Crops**  
- Primary calibration will use full master images; they provide the most accurate color reference.  
- If the specialist rejects master images, we will provide cropped sections that exclude donor text while preserving color data.  
- Any alternative must be approved in writing before use.

**3. Scan Correction Window**  
- Studio has 10 business days after delivery to correct scans, adjust color, and finalize master files.  
- Corrections are logged; any changes after this window require a new correction request and timeline.

**4. Backup Rotation**  
- Backups are created daily for the first 45 days of the pilot.  
- After day 45, the oldest backup set is retired and may be deleted; the most recent set is retained.  
- Deletion of retired backups is documented and confirmed.

**5. Publication of Process Image**  
- We propose publishing an anonymized process image that shows scanning workflow without any donor content.  
- Any image containing donor text or identifiers requires written donor consent before publication.  
- Consent forms will be retained for the duration of the pilot and archived per the retention schedule.

**6. Access and Deletion Schedule**  
| Role | Access Rights | Duration | Deletion Trigger |
|------|---------------|----------|------------------|
| Internal digitization team | Read/write access to master files and QC copies | 30 days from pilot start | After final approval or at 90 days, whichever occurs first |
| External color specialist | Read‑only access to master images (or approved crops) | 20 days from delivery | Upon completion of calibration or earlier if rejected |
| QC files (internal) | Read/write for review | 10 days after delivery | Automatic deletion after 10 days unless extended in writing |
| All pilot data | No access | N/A | Deleted within 5 business days after final approval or at 90 days from pilot start, whichever is later |

- Access is granted via role‑based permissions; all access attempts are logged.  
- Deletion is performed by the studio’s data manager and confirmed in writing.

**7. Logging and Oversight**  
- A detailed access log (who, what, when) is maintained for the entire pilot period.  
- Deletion confirmations are recorded and shared with the archive.  
- Any deviation from the schedule must be approved in writing before implementation.

**Next Steps**  
- Please review the above terms and indicate any required adjustments or additional constraints.  
- If you approve, we can proceed to draft formal NDAs and consent forms for the specialist and any donors.  
- We are ready to schedule a brief call to finalize the schedule and address any outstanding concerns.

The archive proposes one access and deletion schedule per batch to replace the conflicting deadlines in sections 1, 3, 4 and 6.

1. **Calibration and access.** The archive will identify the two restricted collections by batch code before intake. Their handwriting and identifying content may be viewed only by the archive and designated studio employees assigned to digitization and QC. Use the archive’s calibration sheet for external color review. If the sheet proves insufficient, the studio may submit a flattened, masked crop from another collection for archive review. Remove all handwriting, identifying details and embedded metadata. External access requires the archive’s prior written approval of both the named specialist and the exact file, plus a signed NDA. Grant view-only access for calibration and prohibit downloads, screenshots and onward sharing. Full masters stay with the designated studio team.

2. **Corrections and deletion.** We can allow 10 business days from the first delivery of each batch for corrections. Corrected delivery does not restart the clock. Revoke specialist access as soon as calibration ends. Delete all studio and specialist copies, including masters, QC files, crops, temporary files and backups, at written batch acceptance or the end of the correction window, whichever comes first. The archive will hold the preservation masters and can supply a file for a later correction under a new written request.

3. **Evidence and incidents.** Keep role-based access logs using batch codes. Within two business days of deletion, the studio’s data manager must provide a dated record identifying the batch, systems covered, deletion method and completion time, together with the specialist’s confirmation that no copies were retained. Before transfer, enter a monitored email address and phone number for each party’s incident contact in the schedule. The studio must notify the archive contact within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized viewing or disclosure, identify affected batches, preserve relevant logs and report containment actions.

4. **Publicity.** The archive may approve an equipment-only photograph. Keep letters, screens displaying files, labels, people and reflections out of frame. Submit the exact photograph, caption and intended outlet for written archive approval before publication. This schedule grants no permission for a broader workflow image.

**Outstanding exception.** Can the studio exclude pilot files from its 45-day backup rotation or delete each batch from every backup by its deadline? If neither is feasible, please identify the affected systems, the shortest guaranteed purge period and who could restore a copy. Any backup exception requires separate written archive approval before the affected materials are transferred.

The archive agrees to use the signed batch-level schedule as the sole schedule governing pilot access, corrections and deletion, subject to two edits.

1. **Specialist access.** Replace “master or crop” with “the archive’s calibration sheet or, if the sheet is insufficient, a flattened, masked crop from a non-donor collection.” Remove the full-master option throughout. The archive must approve the named specialist and exact file in writing before view-only access begins, and the specialist must sign the NDA. Neither restricted collection may supply a specialist crop. Revoke access when calibration ends or the batch deletion deadline arrives, whichever comes first.

2. **Backups.** The studio is responsible for confirming whether its systems can exclude pilot files from rotation or purge every copy by the batch deletion deadline. **The 30-day fallback remains unapproved.** If an exception is needed, identify the affected systems and batches, who can technically restore files, and a guaranteed final purge date measured from the earlier of written acceptance or expiry of the 10-business-day correction window. Acceptance may never arrive. Any exception requires separate written archive approval before transfer of the affected batch and a deletion record after the final purge.

**Revised Batch‑Level Schedule (incorporating archive edits and restored access clause)**  

1. **Access to Full Masters and Restricted Content**  
   - Only the archive and designated studio digitization and QC staff may view full masters or restricted donor content.  
   - The studio logs each access attempt by user, batch code, and time.  

2. **Specialist Access**  
   - Specialist may receive **only** the archive’s calibration sheet **or**, if the sheet is insufficient, a flattened, masked crop from a non‑donor collection.  
   - Archive must approve the named specialist **and the exact file** in writing before any view‑only access begins.  
   - Specialist signs NDA; access is view‑only via a secure portal; downloads, screenshots, and onward sharing prohibited.  
   - Access is revoked immediately when calibration ends **or** when the batch deletion deadline arrives, whichever occurs first.  

3. **Corrections**  
   - Studio has 10 business days from the first delivery of the batch to correct scans, adjust color, and finalize masters. Corrected delivery does not restart the clock.  

4. **Deletion**  
   - Upon written batch acceptance **or** at the end of the 10‑day correction window (whichever occurs first), studio deletes all copies: masters, QC files, crops, temporary files, and backups.  
   - Archive retains preservation masters and may supply a file for later correction under a new written request.  

5. **Backup Exception Requirements**  
   - Studio must confirm in writing **whether it can exclude pilot files from the 45‑day rotation** or purge every copy by the batch deletion deadline.  
   - **If neither is feasible**, studio must identify:  
     - Affected backup systems and batches  
     - Every role that can technically restore a copy (including studio or provider administrators)  
     - A guaranteed final purge date measured from the earlier of (a) written acceptance or (b) expiry of the 10‑business‑day correction window  
   - Any exception requires separate written archive approval before the affected batch is transferred.  
   - After the final purge, studio must provide a deletion record confirming no copies remain.  
   - **No backup extension has been approved.**  

6. **Incident Management**  
   - Both parties provide monitored email and phone incident contacts before any transfer.  
   - Within 2 business days of deletion, studio’s data manager submits a dated record (batch, systems, deletion method, completion time) plus specialist confirmation that no copies remain.  
   - Studio must notify archive contact within 24 hours of any suspected loss, unauthorized viewing, or disclosure; identify affected batches; preserve logs; and report containment actions.  

7. **Publicity**  
   - Only an equipment‑only photograph (no letters, screens, labels, people, or reflections) may be published. Exact photograph, caption, and outlet require written archive approval. No donor consent forms are required for this photograph.  

**Request for Confirmation**  
- Please provide written confirmation of the studio’s ability to exclude pilot files from the 45‑day backup rotation **or** purge every copy by the batch deletion deadline.  
- If neither is feasible, submit the details required in section 5 above.  
- Upon receipt, the archive will hold the affected batch pending separate written approval for any backup exception.
